title: Book 15 opens: stand before God washed; cleansing in Christ
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK FIFTEEN. That one must stand beside God clean and washed-out, and that in Christ again the cleansing is for us.
Cyril: From every side for us, O Palladius, there has been gathered a clear and vivid proof of word, of the needing to go
translator_notes: Ends mid ἰέναι into §2 παγκάλως; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Enter God’s house washed; all have sinned; God wipes iniquities
english: Cyril: …most beautifully into a house of God, both bright and washed-out, and gaining the familiarity toward him through sanctification. For then we will meet with a gracious God, and that we may speak thus, with a whole eye looking the things according to us, and distributing the sparing most fitting for the holy ones. ‘And upon whom will I look,’ he says, ‘but upon the humble and quiet and trembling at my words?’ For truly holy hands will he stretch-up, and somehow unto the ear itself of the divinity will he cry-through, the one having thus, so as also having arrived unto an end of what things he might somehow pray, from over-joy to say: ‘He heard from his holy temple my voice, and my cry before him will go into his ears.’ Or did you not learn clearly with the all-divine David singing-up for us, that ‘Eyes of Lord are upon righteous ones, and his ears unto their entreaty’?
Palladius: I learned.

Cyril: That the word is true, it is not lawful to doubt, yet, upon at least the needing to rub-off defilements, what manner would there be by us? for no one will understand transgressions, and many things we all stumble. And the nature is sick with the easy unto sin, and is very easily-beside unto the having been natural to do-injustice, with the inclination unto the worthless somehow smoothing for us the way of the outlandish and abominable pleasure.
Palladius: You speak well; for I would agree having delayed nothing, for the one having chosen to speak-rightly.

Cyril: For already also the flesh from earth has been sick in itself with the law of the sin, and very easily-carried-aside is the human mind, unto the needing to turn-aside unto the evil things from youth, according to the having-been-written. Therefore also a sacred word is gloomy-upon for us justly: ‘For all,’ he says, ‘turned-aside, together they became useless, there is not one doing kindness, there is not until one.’ And since God is as you, lifting-out lawlessnesses, and stepping-over injustices for the leftovers of his inheritance, and he did not hold unto a witness his wrath, because he is a willer of mercy?’ And another again: ‘Remember these, Jacob and Israel, do not forget me. For behold I wiped-out as in a cloud your lawlessnesses, and as mist your sins.’ And very many things one might collect the
translator_notes: Ends mid τὰ into §3 ἀπὸ τῆς θείας; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Legal images of cleansing; unblemished offerings type Christ/us
english: Cyril: …from the divine Writing, showing very well the true at least in these for us, and the, for which both clear and vivid the faith would follow, to heap-on other things, superfluous I think somehow.
Palladius: But vivid on the one hand that the matter, clear for everyone. Yet I at least would choose, also from legal images to look-through the cleansing in Christ.

Cyril: So then observe, if it is dear to you, and it seems for us to go thus; for the having-been-defiled, and those having been borne-under by charges of lawlessness, the law was ordering to sacrifice, distinguishing twofold the manners of the sacrifices. For some write-down Emmanuel being slaughtered over us ourselves, and others also us ourselves dying to the world, and bringing-up unto a smell of sweet-fragrance for God the own life and salvation. Or will we not, deadening the members the upon the earth, and freeing the mind of worldly carrying-around and of more earthy pleasures, live-through the divine and evangelical life?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: So then a sacrifice is, the spiritual thorough-cleansing as in death of Christ, and a prayer and gift, as by us, the dedicating to God the good-order and life in holiness. And the law pre-distinguishes and witnesses clearly, the needing to make the approaches at least in these unblemished, both usefully and necessarily. And since of the being-brought-forward victims, some were signaling Christ, as being slaughtered over us, and some also type us, all but sacrificing-up for God the own life. In this way he says, they must both be unblemished, and according to no manner sick with the defect. For unblemished is Christ; for he did not do sin, but neither would God receive us ourselves, being still in defilements, and sick with the unpleasing of the sin. It has been written… ‘a vow, or according to choice or in your feasts, from the herds or from the sheep, unblemished it will be acceptable, every blemish will not be in it. Blind or crushed, or tongue-cut, or warted, or mangy, or having lichens, they will not bring these forward to God, and unto a fruit-offering you will not give from them upon the altar to the Lord. And a calf or a sheep ear-cut,’
translator_notes: Ends mid ὠτότμητον into §4; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Male unblemished = Christ; blind/crushed/tongue-cut manners
english: Cyril: …or dock-tailed you will make them slaughters for yourself; and unto your vow it will not be received. A crushed one and squeezed-out, and a eunuch, and pulled-apart, you will not bring them forward to the Lord, and upon your land you will not make. And from a hand of an alien-born you will not bring-forward the gifts of your God from all these, because corruptions are in them, and a blemish in them. These will not be received for you.’ So then observe that the law enjoins clearly and openly, both for those from blood of Israel, and for those outside and having been judged-into unto peoples, I say the proselytes, the needing to blemish-inspect very well the sacred things. For he said needing to be brought-up by us the male and unblemished, that is, the well-strong, and above passions; for the softness, and mindset the female-fitting, and indeed also the being sick with the inward and intelligible defect at least unto mind, is altogether unacceptable to God, and rejectable. Or do you not say unholy is the one for whom these would appear present?
Palladius: For how not?

Cyril: So then rejectable on the one hand the strengthless, and the as it were relaxed, and acceptable the well-strong, as being painted in a nature of males, if it should have yoked-beside the unblemished. And such would be unto a clear type for us of Christ. For male together and unblemished is Emmanuel, if at least he is truly power of God, and not knowing sin. And male also otherwise; for always preeminent, and in better things than the other is the male; and toward this at least also most leadership-holding. And he has stood-before and is incomparably in better things, and leads the wholes, even if the Son has become according to us, and the shepherd has been reckoned among sheep usefully. And unholy and sendable-away of the victims, blind, and crushed, and indeed also tongue-cut, and warted, and mangy, and lichen… So then the word upon each, and what would become clarify again.

Cyril: So then I am somehow also very eagerly. So then blind seems to say the unwise and unintelligent, and not having divine light in himself that is, the enlightenment through Christ in Spirit, and altogether unholy, the still mindless and unfaithful; ‘For if you should not believe, you will not understand,’ he says. And crushed
translator_notes: Ends mid Συντετριμμένον into §5; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Crushed = wholly sick; tongue-cut = cannot confess; wart/mange growing sin
english: Cyril: …again, the one having been sick wholly, and having healthy altogether nothing, nor indeed being able to walk-straight, or being strong to do some of the good things, and being altogether worsted of the well-strength in Christ and in Spirit, and something such have suffered, those about whom it has been written, through one of the holy prophets: ‘Thus says Lord: Behold I give upon this people a weakness, and they will be weak in it fathers and sons together; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.’ But the divine Melodist for us has brought-in cheerful those having been justified in the faith the in Christ, both psalming and saying: ‘Bless, my soul, the Lord, the one healing all your diseases, the one ransoming from corruption your life.’ And tongue-cut, as I at least think, the one not knowing to speak-rightly, nor indeed being strong to cry-up the word of the faith which we proclaim according to the having-been-written, the question from a good conscience unto God, yet that also such a disease again they will beat-off, in a presence of Christ, the prophet will clarify saying: ‘And tongues the stammering will quickly learn to speak peace.’ So then tongue-cut the still stammering, and not yet having been taught to speak the peace from above for us and from Father, that is, Christ, or the things upon him. And warted and mangy, and having lichens we say those, who ever would have at least in themselves a passionate mind, and having been sick-in with much the corruption in sins, not indeed that one must also lead them toward the lesser thinking-through, but rather releasing them to creep-through unto the more shameful, and to be widened toward the worse. For a wart and a wild mange, and indeed also a lichen, always appear going toward increase, and having been distributed toward having worse… those in a reputation on the one hand of manliness the unto virtue, not indeed still also energetic toward boasts of virtue, and dry as it were and fruitless, and having been taken-away many-manneredly from the being able to bear-fruit. For as great as most a people of unholy passions forces us unto the strengthless and inactive, and still with this the not being strong to bear-fruit. In this way, as I at least think, also with many names the
translator_notes: Ends mid τὸ into §6 εὐνουχισθέν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Eunuch names = passions; only through Christ; leaven honey salt
english: Cyril: …having-been-eunuched the law calls-out; for a crushed one, he says, and squeezed-out, and a eunuch and pulled-apart; for all-variegated are the passions in us, leading as it were through a long path unto the strengthless and inactive.’
Palladius: Persuasive the word.

Cyril: And abominable that beside these it is, also through an alien hand, to sacrifice-down the sacred-works for God, he further-showed saying: ‘And from a hand of an alien-born you will not bring-forward the gifts to Lord your God.’ Through which it is signaled typically, that through Christ alone is the Father approachable; for he himself is our truly unblemished and great high priest, the mediator economically; for as the all-divine Paul writes: ‘In him we have had the approach in Spirit toward the Father.’ So then of blemish must have been freed those who ever would choose to dedicate their own souls to God and Father, with Christ mediating; ‘For holy you will be,’ he says, ‘just as I am holy.’
Palladius: Most excellently you spoke.

Cyril: And having rhythm-set the manners of the sacrifice, as in cattle and sheep, also through other thoughts for us he comes, enjoining very well the needing to approach God unblemishedly for those accustomed to do this; for he said again in Leviticus: ‘Every sacrifice which if you should bring-forward to Lord, you will not bring-forward leavened; for every leaven and every honey you will not bring-forward from it, to fruit-offer to Lord, a gift of firstfruit you will bring them forward to Lord, upon the altar it will not be brought-up unto a smell of sweet-fragrance to Lord, and every gift of your sacrifice will be salted with salt. You will not pause salts of a covenant to Lord from your sacrifices, upon every gift of you you will bring-forward salt to Lord your God.’ So then leaven would be a type of craftiness, not altogether also only of the blamed, but also of the other, I say the good and praised, which also of the wisdom… needing to be brought unto a fruit-offering and sacrifice, both leaven and honey. For he receives on the one hand from the one bringing-forward unto a gift and firstfruit, yet brings-up nowhere unto a smell of sweet-fragrance for God.
Palladius: Then what the riddle clarify again.
Cyril: Hard-to-reach, O Palladius, is the matter. For what would it wish to signal, the making these nowhere rejectable, not indeed still also unto a fruit-offering and sacri-
translator_notes: Ends mid θυ into §7 σίαν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Craftiness vs simplicity; honey = marriage; salt = gracious word
english: Cyril: …fice to bring them up, how is it not uphill to see? So then I think that also crafty sometimes of a holy and good soul, if it should be seen according to seasons, and should have a pretext the piety unto God, not rejectable on the one hand beside him, yet not in equal word will it be ranked of the sweet-fragrant virtue, nor would it be reckoned unto the intelligible sacrifice. For simplicity rather is more honored beside God. For the sacred Writing wonders-down at the all-divine Jacob, saying thus: ‘And Jacob was an unmolded man, dwelling in a house.’ For craftiness has been marked-off from all the unhurtful ones. And toward at least the holy apostles the Savior himself was saying: ‘Become prudent as the snakes, and unmixed, as the doves.’ But the unmixed is honorable beside God, and according to another somehow of all in better things. And the crafty and wicked, fitting for the management of the apostleship, which also the blessed Paul was using according to seasons, fleeing-through everywhere the premature enduring death from enemies. So then the crafty at least in the eager-acts according to God, acceptable on the one hand would become, yet would be reckoned nowhere unto a sweet-fragrance of virtue, if it should be assayed according to own nature. According to the equal manner also the honey, having been taken-beside unto a type of the fleshly pleasure, would under-show, I think somehow, this worldly life, and not having been freed from fleshly pleasures; for honorable is marriage, serving the child-bearings, and unchargeable according to law, the one having been used in Christ. Yet this will not be for some unto a power of virtue, nor indeed will it be ranked in equal with the boasts of continence; and the blessed Paul also writes to those in marriage: ‘Do not separate from one another, unless somehow from agreement unto a season, in order that you may have leisure for the prayer and the entreaty.’ And again… to the holy disciples he was saying. And Paul also writes: ‘Your word in grace and having been seasoned with salt, in order that it may give grace to those hearing.’
Palladius: So then it has been fitted that the thoughtful and graceful is signaled through the salts.

Cyril: Thus it holds; and I think needing thereafter having distinguished very well the manners upon at least the needing to sacrifice-down, from the sacred Writings themselves already to look-down, the
translator_notes: Ends mid τὸ into §8 ὅπως; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Sin-offering calf for anointed priest; cleansing in Christ for all
english: Cyril: …how there would become for those having been sick-through with the sin, to slip-out of the disease, and to beat-off the damages from the faulting; so then it has been written in Leviticus: ‘And Lord spoke toward Moses, saying: Speak toward the sons of Israel, saying: A soul if it should sin opposite Lord unwillingly, from all the commands of Lord, which one must not do and should do one something from them; if on the one hand the high priest the having-been-anointed should sin so as for the people to sin, also he will bring-forward about his sin, which he sinned, a calf from cattle unblemished to the Lord about the sin. And he will bring-forward the calf beside the door of the tent of the witness opposite Lord, and will put his hand upon the head of the calf opposite Lord, and will slaughter the calf before Lord. And the priest the christ the having-been-perfected the hands having taken from the blood of the calf, also will bring it into the tent of the witness; and the priest will dip the finger into the blood, and will sprinkle from the blood seven times opposite Lord, according to the holy veil. And the priest will put from the blood of the calf upon the horns of the altar of the incense of the composition the opposite Lord, which is in the tent of the witness. And all the blood of the calf he will pour-out beside the base of the altar of the whole-burnt-offerings, which is beside the doors of the tent of the witness. And all the fat of the calf of the of the sin, he will take-around from it the fat the covering the inwards, and all the fat the upon the inwards, and the two kidneys, and fat the upon them, which is upon the thighs, and the lobe the upon the liver with the kidneys he will take-around it, which manner it is taken-away from the calf of the sacrifice of the salvation… him according to the equal type to the first, very well he says.
Palladius: So then what again would be at least in these the word?

Cyril: Clear, O Palladius, and not hard to take, for those at least altogether sound-minded. For in Christ is the cleansing of priests, and of people, of small and great, and summarily of all, and if according to one somehow faulting we should be caught, through at least the not knowing the divine law,
translator_notes: Ends mid νόμον into §9 ἤγουν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Christ the calf at tent door; blood sprinkling; outside gate = world
english: Cyril: …or somehow having been forced unwillingly, unto at least the least seeming good to God the Master of all. In this way also the all-divine David was sounding-upon for us: ‘Sins of my youth and of my ignorance do not remember.’ And as being good by nature, both kind and pity-loving and not having been ignorant of the strengthless of our nature, all but also the blessed Job clearly charges, both about to and drawing-back toward releasing for some the sins. And he says thus: ‘And why did you not make a forgetting of my lawlessness, and a cleansing of my sin?’ So then the law cries-up-further, that in Christ and in him alone those held-in by the sins will be justified through faith. For he himself is the one as a calf being sacrificed over us beside the doors of the sacred and divine tent, in order that he may widen-out for us the entrance unto the inside, he himself the one lifting our sins, according to the prophet’s voice. For this I think to signal, the putting the hands upon the calf, he himself the one having gone-in through the blood into the Holies of holies, and having found for us a holy ransoming, and by one offering having perfected unto the continual those being sanctified, according to the voice of the blessed Paul; he himself is the one in the sprinkling of his own blood sanctifying the Church, and this richly. ‘For the priest will dip,’ he says, ‘the finger into the blood, and will sprinkle from the blood seven times with the finger opposite Lord.’—‘For we have come-near,’ he says, ‘to a heavenly Jerusalem, and to a Church of firstborn ones having been written-up in heavens, and to a blood of sprinkling speaking better, than Abel.’ For the blood of Abel was crying-down toward God, condemning of the murderer, and the precious blood of Christ the Savior of us all, speaks about us the better things toward God. … And the most sacred Paul was signaling the outside of the gate, the outside of the world to think. For the wishing to follow Christ stands us out of worldly life. And Paul will witness again. For he said thus about Christ: ‘Through whom for me a world has been crucified, and I to the world.’ And walking upon the earth the holy ones are eager to live-through no longer earthily, but rather to have in heaven the citizen-
translator_notes: Ends mid πολί into §10 τευμα; PG mid-cut kept. No speaker tags in this column slice.

title: Ash-water cleansing; calf for ruler/people; kid for one; grace abounds
english: Cyril: …ship. And a cleansing for the having-been-defiled, the ash-heap with water. For a releasing of sin, the passion of the Savior, sanctifying us through water, through which we will gain not a putting-away of filth of flesh, according to the having-been-written, but the washing-off of the defilements in souls; ‘For wash yourselves,’ he says, ‘and become clean;’ and a prophetic word from above was ordering for us.
Palladius: So then in a calf as in an image and types, the death of Christ through us and over us is being sketched.
Cyril: You understand very well, and toward this at least you would wonder-down, I think, also looking unto that.
Palladius: The of what sort?

Cyril: For if on the one hand the leader together of those yoked-under should sin, or then the under-hand multitude itself according to itself, a calf will be the victim. And with a leader having been caught in special stumblings, let him bring-up, he says, a he-goat from goats. And if somehow someone should be of those in peoples, male no longer, but female let the slaughter be; And I will read, if it seems good, also the laws upon these, for he said thus: ‘And if the ruler should sin, and should do one from all the commands of Lord his God, which will not be done unwillingly, and should fault, and the sin should be known to him, which he sinned in it, also he will bring-forward his gift a he-goat from goats, male unblemished, about sin; and he will put the hand upon the head of the he-goat, and they will slaughter him in a place, where they slaughter the whole-burnt-offerings before Lord, it is of sin. And the priest will put from the blood of the of the sin with the finger upon the horns of the altar of the whole-burnt-offerings, and all his blood he will pour-out beside the base of the altar of the whole-burnt-offerings, and all his fat he will bring-up upon the altar, just as the fat of a sacrifice of salvation, and he will propitiate about… approach of victims; and a calf on the one hand was over both ruler and people, somehow common and having been sick with one sin. And one kid, over one, or of one soul; for Christ has brought himself forward, on the one hand over all, as in an image in the calf, a heavy and great victim; ‘For where the sin abounded,’ he says, ‘the grace over-abounded.’ And of a kid and of a sheep
translator_notes: Ends mid προβά into later §§; tip §§1-10.
